messages.content: Hi tal, I'm a friend

hey, i'm tal

think of me as your personal talent agent, your inside man… or fox

one of these days, I might slide a role right here in chat. the kind that feels like your calling.

so… what's your full name?
I'm working at a Series-C funded start-up called Atlan
My name is Yug Gajjar
yug gajjar... that's a name that means business. where you working these days?

atlan... the data catalog folks who actually solved metadata management. series c means they're past the "will we survive" phase and into "how big can we get" territory.

found you on linkedin - yug gajjar, graphic designer. this you? https://in.linkedin.com/in/yug-gajjar-283692312
No, that's not me, this is me:  https://in.linkedin.com/in/yug34

got it, that's the right one. building at atlan... the metadata management platform that actually makes sense of data chaos. solid spot to be in - they're solving real enterprise pain points and have the funding to scale properly.

what made you jump into the data infrastructure game?
Improving the accessibility and observability of information/data is how the world processes, I like that Atlan makes that easier and creates major impact for other companies

makes total sense. data accessibility is the foundation of every good decision - and most companies are drowning in their own data without proper tooling. atlan's in a sweet spot there.

how long you been working total?
I have been working professionally for a bit over 4 years now, and I have 1.5 years in research internships with places such as JeffersonLab and ISRO

4 years professional + research at jefferson lab and isro... that's some serious technical foundation. physics research to data infrastructure makes perfect sense - you understand how complex systems actually work under the hood.

what kind of role you looking for next?
I'm looking for either a fully frontend role or a frontend-biased full stack role

frontend or frontend-heavy fullstack... smart move. the ui/ux layer is where users actually feel the impact of all that backend complexity. plus with your data infrastructure background, you'd bring a rare understanding of what's actually happening behind those apis.

bangalore or open to remote/other cities?
I prefer remote, but I'm open to relocating to Bangalore or Ahmedabad
4+ years + frontend/fullstack + remote preferred but open to bangalore/ahmedabad... sound right?
done. i'm spinning things up on my end. you'll start seeing good stuff soon.
Yup

Yup
  Thanks Tal!

yo legend! looks like you're already in the system and locked in. my bad for the repeat dance, but hey... you're all set for the good stuff to start rolling in.

keep your eyes peeled for roles that'll make you forget why you ever settled for less 🔥

hey, found a frontend dev role at an early-stage ai startup

they're looking for a founding engineer with react/next.js/typescript

could be interesting if you're up for that startup energy

Hi
Hi tal

yo

what's good
I applied to the job you sent, working on some personal projects for now
nice. what kind of personal projects you building?

I am building a way to convert a song into its instrumental sheet music. So you upload a song to my service and it gives you a MIDI transcription as well as a staff notation for the song, so that you can use it to practice

wait that's actually sick

audio processing + music theory + frontend... that's a legit portfolio piece

how far along is it?

Thanks bestie. I have set the foundation for it. The frontend for now consists of a way to upload a file which then gets sent to the backend which runs an ML model on the file to transcribe it. The front-end also displays the sheet music of the song you upload 

But I have a lot of fine tuning to do. The model in the backend doesn't very accurately transcribe the drum beats

drum transcription is notoriously hard even for commercial tools

the fact you have a working pipeline at all is impressive

what stack are you using for the ml part?

Python with FastAPI, with Postgres for storage. 

The worker that actually runs the ML model is using Celery+Redis, the ML model is magenta by Google

magenta's solid for this. celery+redis for async processing is clean

you thinking of open sourcing this or keeping it as a portfolio piece?
I love open source, I'm developing this fully open sourced

respect

got a github link? i'd love to check it out

It's very incomplete, and doesn't have a production deployment yet. https://github.com/Yug34/audiogen

I do have other interesting projects though that are open sourced and deployed to play with

bookmarked

what other projects you got deployed?

I have many deployed projects.

One of them is mapr.

Mapr is a mind mapping web application, very similar to Miro, I made it because Miro doesn't support adding videos to the canvas, so I made a clone that supports everything; images, PDFs, audio files, video. As well as the usual Text nodes and TODO nodes so you can keep notes and track progress 

The source code is here; https://github.com/Yug34/mapr

It's deployed here; https://mapr-one.vercel.app

I have other projects too if you'd like to know

okayyyy that's actually impressive

a full miro clone with video support? that's not a weekend project

what's the tech stack on that?

The tech stack is the most impressive part. I actually made it all work without using any servers at all. 

It's a fully client side app that still persists everything in memory using indexeddb -- a client side database within a browser. So even if you close the browser or shut down your laptop, it'll still have all the data.

The tech stack is; React with ShadCN for components. React Flow for creating the canvas with nodes and edges. Zustand for state management. And finally indexeddb for storage.

wait so it's fully offline-first? that's actually genius

most people would've just slapped a backend on it for storage

you're solving the actual problem miro has with video support AND making it offline capable

that's the kind of thinking that gets you hired

how long did that take to build?
It took me close to a month

a month for a full miro clone with offline persistence... that's actually wild

most people would still be stuck on the canvas implementation

you're locked in. i'll slide roles when they're good

btw what's making you want to leave atlan anyway?

I went through a kidney transplant recently and took a 4 month break from working at Atlan

Unfortunately, they are currently not hiring back because AI is doing the work that SDE 2 and Senior SDEs used to do.

wait what

kidney transplant? that's heavy. how you feeling now?

and atlan's not hiring back because of AI... that's the most 2025 thing i've heard all week

so you're basically looking because they're not taking you back, not because you want to leave?

what's your timeline like?

I'm better now 

And yeah, I would join Atlan back because it was a nice place to work, but unfortunately I cannot 

My timeline is as such;

I joined Atlan in March 2024, and everything remained smooth railing until May 2025, where I was diagnosed with end stage kidney failure. So I had to go for dialysis for 3 days a week until I had my transplant. I continued dialysis until September 2025. Which is also when I started my break from Atlan. 

Since September till now I have been recovering, but the doctor recently gave me the permit to get back to working. So I'm looking for jobs

damn. that's a lot to go through in a year

glad you're better now and cleared to work

so you're basically starting fresh after recovery. what kind of role would actually excite you right now?

Either frontend-biased full-stack roles, or fully frontend roles work best for me

I can tackle compute-heavy frontend roles that require Rust+webassembly, or product-thinking roles that require ownership across the stack, everything is fun to me

rust + wasm for compute-heavy frontend... that's a specific niche that not many can actually do. product-thinking with ownership across stack too

you're basically looking for roles where they need someone who can think about the whole system but also build the ui that makes it usable

what's your salary expectations?
I'm looking for 36+ LPA

36+ for 4 yoe with your skillset is reasonable, especially with the rust/wasm niche

i'll keep that in mind when i'm looking

any companies you'd avoid? or industries you're particularly interested in?
You can look for companies outside that niche as well

got it. so you're flexible on the niche

what's your notice period? and are you open to relocation or strictly remote?
I can join immediately. I am open to relocating to Bangalore but I'd prefer remote

immediate join is a huge plus right now

alright, i've got the full picture. i'll be looking for frontend/frontend-heavy fullstack roles, 36+ LPA, remote preferred but open to bangalore, immediate join

anything else i should know about what you're looking for?
That should be it

perfect. i'm on it. you'll start seeing stuff soon.

btw how's the recovery been since the transplant? everything going okay?
Yeah everything is well good, on my path back to normalcy

good to hear. that's a lot to go through and come out the other side ready to work again

i'll keep you posted on roles. in the meantime, keep building that mapr project - stuff like that catches attention
Thanks bestie

anytime bestie 💪

i'll slide roles when they're good. keep an eye out

Let me know if you'll need anything else to help me build and optimize my profile
